blind_target.authors: Asimovic N, Nagler J, Bonneau R, et al.
blind_target.title: Testing the effects of Facebook usage in an ethnically polarized setting
blind_target.evidence_quote: To explore this question, we replicate the only published study to date that tests the effects of social media cessation on interethnic attitudes (Asimovic et al., 2021).
blind_target.outcome_quote: We are not able to replicate the main effect found in Asimovic et al. (2021): in Cyprus, we cannot reject the null hypothesis of no effect. We do, however, find a significant interaction between the heterogeneity of users’ offline networks and the deactivation treatment within our 2021 subsample, consistent with the pattern from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The main effect fails, while the moderation and anxiety findings agree. The main-effect statement is not an overall verdict.

blind_target.evidence_quote:
Several independent research groups have observed
that P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the

AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]. These

observations reinforce a hypothetical recessive model

for the P86L variant in AD. So, we decided to evalu-

ate this model in AAO in Spanish AD patients.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Both results

are compatible with the original ﬁndings [1], although
the observed genetic model for the P86L mutation in

Spanish series seems different. In fact, we observed a

recessive instead a dominant model as originally pro-

posed.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Outcome follows the explicit comparisons; the disease-risk nulls of prior replication papers are not themselves the age-at-onset claims re-tested here.
